problem: The code computes `grant = (ts1 > ts2 ? ts1 : ts2) + 1;` which selects the larger timestamp (7) and adds 1, contradicting the described rule that the lock must be granted to the node with the smallest timestamp (Node1 with ts = 5). The printed message also mixes the decision (grant to Node1) with the logical‑time calculation, making the algorithm unclear.
fix: Use the smallest timestamp to decide which node receives the lock and compute the new logical time after the lock is released. For example: int ts1 = 5, ts2 = 7; int grant_node = (ts1 < ts2) ? 1 : 2; // 1 = Node1, 2 = Node2 int new_time = (ts1 > ts2 ? ts1 : ts2) + 1; // logical time after receipt printf("Lock granted to Node%d at logical time %d\n", grant_node, new_time); This prints "Lock granted to Node1 at logical time 8" and follows the rule of granting to the smallest timestamp.
